text:
samir: Quick FYI — I’m planning a small infra tweak for inference-api: switching the k8s config to a partitioned rolling update so we can bump replicas from 4 -> 6 without knocking all pods at once. Also a tiny terraform change to how we reference the runtime secret (moving to module-level secret lookup). Can people do a quick sanity check on risks (PVCs, HPA, readiness) before I open the PR?

linh: quick q — are we changing a Deployment or a StatefulSet for this? PVCs only matter if it’s a STS.

samir: Deployment. No persistent volumes for inference-api; model cache is ephemeral on pod FS. StatefulSet not involved.

jess: ok good. main things to watch: readinessProbe + app warmup. If we ramp replicas up while readiness is slow we might hit CPU/memory spikes and HPA will react. What are the probe settings?

samir: probes are 1s initialDelay, 3s period, handler is /health (simple). The model warmup happens on first request, we added a preheat path but it’s async. I was thinking partitioned rollout with partition=2 to keep 2 old pods while we bring new ones up.

kai: FYI partitioned approach is fine. Two suggestions: 1) set maxUnavailable to 20% rather than 10% so rollout doesn’t stall waiting for old pods to terminate; 2) add a preStop hook to sleep 10s to give connections a chance to drain.

samir: good call on preStop. Will add:
```yaml
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 10"]
```

linh: also callout for terraform side — you said module-level secret lookup change. Make sure we don’t change resource names for the k8s_secret resource or it will force recreate. If you only change the value reference, plan should be no-op for k8s_secret.

samir: pasting the diff from my local terraform plan (sanitized):
```diff
- resource "kubernetes_secret" "runtime_config" {
-   metadata { name = "inference-runtime" }
-   data = { config = module.runtime.default }
- }
+ resource "kubernetes_secret" "runtime_config" {
+   metadata { name = "inference-runtime" }
+   data = { config = var.runtime_secret_lookup == "module" ? module.runtime.default : var.runtime_secret }
+ }
```

devops-bot: terraform plan: 1 to change, 0 to add, 0 to destroy (inferences-infra).

jess: that conditional is fine. Just double-check CI secret encryption step — we need to ensure the string is KMS-wrapped if it comes from var. Otherwise ops will complain.

ops-oncall: Also flag for traffic shifting: if the service has sticky sessions or client-side pinning to pod IPs, partitioning can leave some clients hitting old pods. Do we have any IP affinity?

samir: no sticky sessions — we use ALB round robin and session cookies are app-layer stateless.

kai: one more thought — HPA minReplicas currently 2. If you bump replicas to 6, HPA might immediately scale down to 2 based on CPU if traffic is low. Consider temporarily scaling HPA minReplicas to 4 during the rollout window.

samir: good idea. I’ll set minReplicas=4 for the rollout PR and then revert after 24h.

jess: lgtm from me, just document the preStop and HPA temporary bump in the PR description.

linh: quick nit — update the rolloutStrategy annotation we use in the chart so the console shows the partition policy: `redwood.io/rollout-strategy: partitioned`. Ops will thank you.

samir: will do. Plan: open small PR tagging @jess and @kai, include terraform plan snippet, add preStop, bump HPA min, update annotation, and include rollback instructions. Hoping to roll tomorrow morning during low traffic.

kai: sounds good, :thumbsup: lgtm.

ops-oncall: I’ll keep an eye on oncall channel during the window, ping me if latency > 200ms.

deploy-bot: scheduled quiet roll for inference-api at 2026-03-18T14:00Z (manual trigger required).

samir: thanks all — PR opened: https://git.redwood/inference/infra/pull/423 (will ping reviewers).
